entries.operational_definition: A latent coordinate representing the current level of disease-specific neurodegenerative process burden. P is a state, not its derivative: instantaneous progression velocity is dP/dt. P must remain distinct from a diagnostic label, a clinical severity score, neuronal integrity, and proteostasis impairment.
entries.working_polarity: Higher = greater latent disease-process burden; dP/dt represents its instantaneous rate of change.

subconstructs.label: Disease pathology burden
subconstructs.description: Disease-specific accumulated pathological process burden, with distinct pathological substrates for Alzheimer disease and Parkinson disease.

subconstructs.label: Trajectory position
subconstructs.description: Position along an individual's latent disease trajectory, separated from the local velocity and from observed clinical function.

overlap_cautions: P must not be defined as a weighted sum of I, M, N, Q and Pr; such a construction would create circularity and undermine identifiability.
The same pathology biomarker may also inform a molecular subconstruct of Pr, but must not be duplicated as independent evidence without a measurement model.
A clinical stage label is not a direct observation of P.

entries.operational_definition: A latent description of central nervous system immune activation, glial response, inflammatory signaling, and resolution processes. Increased I denotes greater neuroimmune activation, not necessarily net neuronal toxicity; protective, reparative, and harmful responses must not be collapsed without evidence.
entries.working_polarity: Higher = greater neuroimmune activation; effect on neuronal integrity may depend on cell state, disease stage, region and context.

subconstructs.label: Microglial state
subconstructs.description: Microglial activation and state transitions, including surveillance, inflammatory, phagocytic and potentially reparative programs.

subconstructs.label: Astrocytic reactivity
subconstructs.description: Astrocytic response states and signaling, which may be protective, reactive or context-dependent.

subconstructs.label: Cytokine and complement signaling
subconstructs.description: Inflammatory cytokine, chemokine and complement pathway activity, with separate source and target cell context.

subconstructs.label: Inflammasome and resolution
subconstructs.description: Inflammasome-associated signaling and counter-regulatory mechanisms involved in resolving or sustaining immune responses.

overlap_cautions: GFAP is a proxy for astrocytic response, not a complete measure of neuroinflammation.
Inflammation may be protective or damaging; a scalar activation burden cannot represent this distinction without additional structure.
Systemic inflammatory markers must not be treated as direct CNS immune-state measurements.

entries.operational_definition: A latent description of neuronal and glial metabolic regulation, energy supply, substrate utilization, lipid handling and redox balance. The top-level M coordinate is a coarse-grained parent construct; its subdomains are not interchangeable measurements and should not be collapsed into one score without a validated aggregation model.
entries.working_polarity: Higher = greater metabolic dysregulation; a more detailed model may require separate bioenergetic, substrate, lipid and redox latent factors.

subconstructs.label: Mitochondrial bioenergetics
subconstructs.description: Mitochondrial respiratory capacity, oxidative phosphorylation, ATP supply and mitochondrial quality-control dependencies.

subconstructs.label: Glucose and lactate metabolism
subconstructs.description: Glucose uptake and utilization, glycolytic activity, lactate production and transport, and metabolic coupling between neural cell types.

subconstructs.label: Lipid metabolism
subconstructs.description: Lipid synthesis, transport, remodeling and utilization, including membrane and lipid-droplet processes.

subconstructs.label: Redox homeostasis
subconstructs.description: NAD redox balance, glutathione systems, reactive oxygen species handling and oxidative stress responses.

overlap_cautions: FDG-PET reflects regional glucose utilization and is not a direct measurement of mitochondrial ATP production or total metabolic health.
Oxidative stress overlaps biologically with inflammation and proteostasis; it must not be counted as three independent measurements.
Mitochondrial and lysosomal processes interact with Pr, so the model must define non-overlapping observation constructs.

entries.operational_definition: A latent description of preserved neuronal viability and structural-functional substrate, including axonal, synaptic and network integrity. Injury markers indicate aspects of damage or turnover and are not direct measurements of all preserved neuronal capacity.
entries.working_polarity: Higher = greater preserved neuronal and circuit integrity.

subconstructs.label: Neuronal viability
subconstructs.description: Cell survival and cellular integrity within disease-relevant neuronal populations and anatomical regions.

subconstructs.label: Axonal integrity
subconstructs.description: Axonal structure and integrity, including degeneration and injury processes.

subconstructs.label: Synaptic integrity
subconstructs.description: Synaptic density, maintenance, transmission substrate and structural remodeling.

subconstructs.label: Network integrity
subconstructs.description: Regional and distributed circuit organization and connectivity relevant to the disease phenotype.

subconstructs.label: Regional neuroanatomical structure
subconstructs.description: Regional morphometric and anatomical measures such as volume, thickness and shape derived from MRI, interpreted as tissue-level structural observations rather than direct neuronal cell counts or functional capacity.

overlap_cautions: NfL is a marker of neuroaxonal injury and is not disease-specific or a direct measurement of preserved neuronal integrity.
Structural MRI atrophy is an indirect tissue-level observation and depends on region, segmentation and acquisition pipeline.
N is not interchangeable with Q: structural integrity and realized function may diverge through reserve, compensation and comorbidity.

entries.operational_definition: A latent description of realized cognitive, motor, non-motor and everyday functional capacity. Q is a phenotype-level construct and may diverge from N because reserve, compensation, environment, treatment and comorbidities modify observed function.
entries.working_polarity: Higher = greater functional capacity; the observed phenotype remains multidimensional and disease-specific.

subconstructs.label: Cognitive function
subconstructs.description: Memory, executive, language, attention, visuospatial and other cognitive capacities relevant to the disease.

subconstructs.label: Motor function
subconstructs.description: Motor performance, gait, dexterity, bradykinesia, rigidity and other disease-relevant movement capacities.

subconstructs.label: Non-motor and autonomic function
subconstructs.description: Sleep, mood, autonomic, sensory and other non-motor capacities and symptoms.

subconstructs.label: Activities of daily living
subconstructs.description: Ability to perform daily tasks and maintain independence, interpreted in the individual's social and environmental context.

overlap_cautions: A single cognitive test or motor scale samples only part of Q.
Q is affected by cognitive reserve, education, treatment, mood, environment and comorbidity; these factors must not be silently interpreted as changes in N.
Alzheimer and Parkinson require different disease-specific functional observation models.

entries.operational_definition: A latent description of protein homeostasis and quality-control capacity, including protein synthesis and folding, chaperone support, trafficking, degradation, autophagy-lysosomal clearance and handling of aggregation-prone species. Increased Pr denotes greater impairment; pathology abundance alone does not measure the full capacity or flux of proteostasis systems.
entries.working_polarity: Higher = greater proteostasis impairment; subdomain-specific capacities and pathological cargo burden may move differently.

subconstructs.label: Folding and chaperone systems
subconstructs.description: Protein folding, refolding, chaperone networks and endoplasmic-reticulum protein quality-control responses.

subconstructs.label: Ubiquitin-proteasome system
subconstructs.description: Ubiquitination, substrate recognition and proteasomal degradation of damaged or unwanted proteins.

subconstructs.label: Autophagy and lysosomal clearance
subconstructs.description: Autophagosome formation and trafficking, lysosomal acidification, cargo degradation and recycling.

subconstructs.label: Aggregation and protein trafficking
subconstructs.description: Handling, transport, seeding, spread and clearance of aggregation-prone proteins, including tau, amyloid-beta and alpha-synuclein in disease-specific contexts.

overlap_cautions: p-tau, amyloid-beta and alpha-synuclein assays measure specific pathological species or seeding activity; they do not directly quantify all proteostasis machinery or its flux.
Autophagy-lysosomal mechanisms overlap with mitochondrial quality control and therefore with M; the constructs must be separated at the observation-model level.
Protein aggregation, protein degradation capacity and aggregate clearance are related but are not the same latent quantity.
